summary: Beaufort County tower: a directory gives 99 ft 9 in, built by the CCC in 1936; 1954 and 1967 survey notes say 110 ft. No source gives its condition today.

facts.design: Four-legged steel girder tower on a concrete foundation
facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources
facts.status_note: No source found says whether the tower still stands.

events.note: Lookout directory entry gives 1936 as the year the Civilian Conservation Corps erected a 99-foot 9-inch steel tower.
Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station as a 110-foot steel tower, with its survey point at the top of the cage.
Army Corps of Engineers recovery note rated the station in good condition and repeated the 110-foot height.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1936 directory entry gives 99 feet 9 inches (about 30.4 m). The 1954 and 1967 survey notes give 110 feet (about 33.5 m). The sources do not explain the difference, so no height is recorded in facts.

sources.title: Datasheet for EY4030 (Everett Forest Service Lot)

notes_for_editor: Height conflicts and is not resolved: 99 ft 9 in (CCC 1936, directory entry) against 110 ft (NGS 1954 and 1967). The directory entry is headed 'Everetts' and gives no coordinates, so its link to the NGS station rests on county and name; the 1967 NGS recovery note does name the station as 'the top of the cage on the Everett Lookout Tower'. No history page, condition after 1967, access or staffing found in any source. Not listed on the National Historic Lookout Register. A search also returned the town of Everetts in Martin County, which is a different place; not used.
